# S2.11 Keep a typed patient name through an Add-patient remount

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | S2 |
| Role | IMPLEMENTATION |
| Level | L1 |
| Contracts | C-ISO@1 |
| Depends | S2.10 |
| Findings | none |
| Confidence | **the emptying is pinned, and S2.10's mechanism for it is disconfirmed.** Fixed decision 5's candidate **S2** said a remount of `AddPatient` reset `name` from `?name=` (`docs/v2/cards/S2.10.md:479-483`); every remount lever in the tree is closed — `web/src/App.tsx:99` is the only key above the routes, `:103` the only `Suspense`, `:122` the only `<Navigate>` in `AppRoutes`, `main.tsx:28` mounts one `path: '*'` route, and a pathname change would **unmount** the dialog rather than re-render it, while the failing run watched `#patient-name` sit on screen for the whole five seconds (`docs/v2/state/reviews/S2.10-impl2.md:129-143`). What the code does show is that `#patient-name` lives inside a subtree the app marks `inert` from its first commit until the primary-window lock is granted (`App.tsx:62`, `:80-88`), and that the grant is followed by a focus move onto `#apunta-content` on **every** cold load (`:248`, `:269-274`) — while Playwright's `fill` on `<input type=text>` is `select()` + `focus()` and then `Input.insertText` into whatever is focused (`@playwright/test` 1.62.1, `node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js`: injected `fill` ends `this.selectText(element); return "needsinput"`, and the server-side `_fill` answers that with `keyboard.insertText`), which does **nothing at all** to an unfocusable element while its only actionability states are `visible`, `enabled`, `editable`. Fixed decision 1 says what to measure, V3's negative control measures it at the base commit, and the fix is at that gate |

## Objective

A name typed into the Add-patient window is still there — in the app, for her,
and in the e2e run — after the window has finished settling behind it.

S2.10 is APPROVED on its objective (**AM-100**,
`docs/v2/state/AMENDMENTS.md:123`) and its spell-check flake is *diagnosed*:
its own new diagnostic at `e2e/tests/spelling.spec.ts:92` fired in the reviewer's
V3 with `Received: ""` and a disabled Add-patient button, i.e. `name` was never
set (`docs/v2/state/reviews/S2.10-impl2.md:126-161`, `:245-256`). S2.10 may not
touch production code, so the fix is this card's, and it is a **product** fix:
on a cold `/patients/new`, Apunta makes itself unfocusable for as long as it
takes the single-primary-window lock to be granted, and then takes the caret
away from the field the dialog had just focused. Fixed decisions 1 and 2 name
the cause, the measurement that pins it, and the two lines that fix it.

The card's objective is the **property**, not the flake: whatever else happens
behind the window — the recency storm, the settings arriving, a focus handoff —
the name she typed stays in the field and stays in her hands. No e2e assertion
is changed to get there; `spelling.spec.ts` is the gate, not the subject.

**The word "remount" in this card's title is the owner's (AM-100) and it is a
disconfirmed hypothesis**, recorded in the Confidence field above rather than
quietly dropped: the fix is not a remount-proofing mechanism, because there is
no remount to survive (Fixed decision 5). The card id and title are not changed
here; if the owner wants the title to match the mechanism, that is §6's.

## Fixed decisions

1. **The cause, and the one measurement that separates it from the remount.**
   The diagnosis, in the order the evidence forced it:
   - **Not a remount.** `AddPatient` is a module-level component rendered by
     `<Route element={<AddPatient />} />` under a `<Suspense>` under one keyed
     `<div>`; the key is `location.pathname` (`App.tsx:99`), the only key above
     it, and the only `Suspense` and the only `<Navigate>` in `AppRoutes` are at
     `:103` and `:122`. `main.tsx:28` mounts a single `path: '*'` data route, so
     no navigation inside the app can re-create `AddPatient` in place. A pathname
     change is the only thing that moves that key, and it takes the
     `/patients/new` match — and therefore the whole dialog — **off the screen**,
     which the failing run contradicts: the locator resolved to
     `<input id="patient-name">` fourteen times across the full five-second
     timeout (`S2.10-impl2.md:136-143`). No provider re-creates its children
     (`SettingsProvider.tsx:142`, `i18n.tsx:90`, `SpellingProvider.tsx:117` — one
     `Provider` each, stable element types), no component in the subtree is
     defined inside another component's body (the class of bug
     `docs/v2/evidence/UI-BATCH2/handoff.md:40-42` records, fixed there and not
     present here), and `SpellLayer` renders its input at a fixed position
     (`SpellLayer.tsx:97-122`).
   - **The gate, which the code does show.** `blocked` is
     `primary.phase !== 'primary'` (`App.tsx:62`) and is written onto
     `#apunta-content` imperatively at `:80-88` — the subtree the whole app
     lives in, the Add-patient window included. The phase starts `'acquiring'`
     (`:194`) and only becomes `'primary'` inside the lock grant (`:361-372`),
     so **on every cold load the app is `inert` from its first commit until the
     grant lands**, and the blocker's own comment says `inert` is there for "a
     non-primary window" (`:74-79`) — a window still deciding is not one.
   - **The keystroke that never arrives.** The failing test's first interaction
     on that page is a `fill` (`spelling.spec.ts:86`), and Playwright's `fill`
     on a text input is `select()` + `focus()` followed by `Input.insertText`
     into the focused element, with `visible`/`enabled`/`editable` as its only
     actionability states (Read). On an element inside an `inert` subtree
     `focus()` is a no-op, so the text is delivered to whatever else holds
     focus and the call still reports success. The value in the field therefore
     stays `""`, the Add-patient button stays disabled because `name` never
     became `'Teh'` (`AddPatient.tsx:150`), and the assertion at `:92` reports
     exactly what the reviewer saw.
   - **Why it is state-dependent, which is the dirty-versus-fresh correlation
     S2.9 measured.** The grant is a promise resolution behind a busy main
     thread: a populated practice loads the patient list, then fires one
     `GET /api/patients/<id>/notes` per patient six at a time
     (`usePatientRecency.ts:24`, `:69`), each completing fetch re-rendering the
     workspace. The longer that storm runs, the longer the window in which the
     field is unfocusable — and the test's `fill` lands within a few
     milliseconds of `goto` returning. A fresh sandbox resolves the grant first;
     a used one often does not (1 of 5 in a used sandbox, 6 of 6 in a fresh one:
     `docs/v2/state/reviews/S2.9-impl.md:206-220`).
   - **And the second half of the same cause, which is the one a user feels.**
     `becomePrimary` computes `wasBlocked = phase !== 'primary'` (`App.tsx:248`),
     which is true on the *initial* grant as well as on a handoff, so the rAF at
     `:269-274` focuses `#apunta-content` on every cold load. Combined with the
     gate — the dialog's own `focus()` at mount was dropped, because it ran
     inside the inert window — the caret is **never** in the name field on a cold
     load, which is the clause `AddPatient.tsx:39-42` asserts and
     `App.test.tsx:816-819` argues nobody can hit.
   - **The third focus move, which the first draft of this decision left out**
     (Read: `App.tsx:490-509`). `PrimaryBlocker` runs a rAF of its own on every
     `[phase, pending]` change and focuses its own dialog div whenever the phase
     is not `'primary'`. It is the sibling rendered after `#apunta-content`, so
     it schedules that frame *after* `Dialog`'s mount focus and the frame runs
     one frame later: on the **fixed** tree, where the name field is focusable
     from its first commit, that frame is what takes the caret back out of the
     field a frame after `Dialog` put it there — and it lives in
     `PrimaryBlocker`, which May edit forbids touching. Its cleanup cancels the
     frame only when the phase changed first,
     so whether it fires is a **race between the grant and one frame** — and
     both answers are real:
     - **fast cold load, the grant lands before that frame.** `:508` cancels it.
       `Dialog`'s mount focus survives, so the post-grant caret on the **fixed**
       tree is the name field; on the base tree `becomePrimary`'s rAF, scheduled
       inside the grant and therefore after the cancel, then focuses
       `#apunta-content`.
     - **slow cold load, the frame wins — the storm case this diagnosis rests
       on.** The caret is on the blocker's dialog div when the grant lands; the
       blocker then returns `null` (`:535`), its DOM is removed, and removing the
       focused element drops the caret to `document.body`. Nothing in the fixed
       tree focuses again after that — that is the whole of decision 2 — so the
       fixed tree's post-grant state is **`body`, not the field**; on the base
       tree `becomePrimary`'s rAF fires last and the state is
       `#apunta-content`.
     So the property the objective names is not "the field holds the caret" but
     **"the app does not move the caret"**: on the fast path the field keeps it,
     on the late path wherever she left it is still there, and on the base tree
     both paths end with the app having moved it. Case (b) pins the late path,
     the one a test can pin deterministically; V5's amplified run covers the
     fast one in a real browser.

   **A real user does lose typed text, and it is not the test's problem to work
   around.** She clicks the name field as the window unblocks and starts typing;
   if the grant's frame lands between her click and the rest of the word — and
   on a loaded practice that frame can be hundreds of milliseconds late, because
   the storm is holding the main thread — the caret moves to the page container
   and the rest of what she typed goes there, leaving the field with a silent
   prefix.

   **The measurement, and it is the card's own negative control (V3), not a
   flake to reproduce.** In the new test file, with a Web Locks shim whose
   `ifAvailable` grant the test holds until it releases it:
   - at the base commit, on a cold `renderApp('/patients/new')`, the content
     subtree is `inert` **while the phase is still `'acquiring'`** — the cause,
     asserted directly, with no dependence on a browser, a dictionary or a
     populated practice; and
   - at the base commit, once the grant is released **and the frame following
     that release has run**, the caret is on `#apunta-content` rather than in the
     name field — the steal, and the thing a user feels. Both halves of that
     sentence are load-bearing and both belong to the case, not to the run: the
     case places the caret in the field itself before the release (decision
     3(b)), and the assertion is taken only after a frame has provably run,
     because `becomePrimary`'s rAF at `:270` and the blocker's at `:505` both do
     their work in a frame. An assertion taken inside the releasing `act()` reads
     the field on the base tree too — the new cases pass, `test $rc -ne 0` is
     false, and Stop condition 1 fires on a correct diagnosis.
    Both must **fail** at the base commit and pass on the fixed tree; that pair is
    what makes the diagnosis a measurement. Neither needs the e2e flake, and
    neither may be replaced by one. Cases (c), (d) and (e) pass at the base and
    must keep passing on the fixed tree — (c) and (e) because they pin behaviour
    the fix must not touch, (d) because the card says so out loud.
   **If both pass at the base commit, the cause is not this and the card stops**
   (Stop condition 1). **If an amplified `spelling.spec.ts` run does fail after
   the fix**, read the trace once and record, at the moment the field reads
   `""`, the value of `document.getElementById('apunta-content').inert` and
   `document.activeElement === document.getElementById('patient-name')`; if the
   gate is closed and the field is focused there, the emptying is a genuine state
   reset and this is Stop condition 2.
2. **The fix is two lines of judgement in `App.tsx`, each narrowing the gate to
   what the gate is for.** The blocker stays exactly as it is; only the two
   reactions to the phase change.
   - **The gate: `inert` while the window is known to be blocked, not while it is
     still finding out.** A window in `'acquiring'` has not been found to be a
     second window, and the code that follows the grant already treats the two
     differently (`:251`). So the `inert` write must apply to `'secondary'` and
     `'unsupported'` — the states the comment at `:74-79` describes — and not to
     `'acquiring'`. **The existing test at `App.test.tsx:1515-1516` must keep
     passing unchanged**: with no Web Locks the phase is `'unsupported'` and
     `content.inert` is still `true`. The blocker keeps covering the screen
     meanwhile (`app.css:2520-2523`, `z-index: 100`) and keeps its own Tab trap
     and Escape handling (`:511-534`), so nothing behind it becomes reachable;
     what changes is that the app behind is no longer removed from the tab order
     and the accessibility tree during the one window in which it is about to be
     the app she is allowed to use.
   - **The caret: move it on a handoff, not on the first grant.** The rAF at
     `:269-274` stays, and it keeps firing for a **takeover** — a window that was
     `'secondary'` and has just been unblocked should land the keyboard back in
     the app, and that is the case it was written for. What must not happen is
     the same move on the `'acquiring'` → `'primary'` grant, where it yanks the
     caret out of a field she is in the middle of typing into. The discriminator
     is already in the file: `phase === 'secondary'` at `:251`, one line above.
     The fix is to use that one and not `wasBlocked`.
   - **What this buys, concretely:** on a cold `/patients/new` the name field is
     focusable from its first commit, `Dialog`'s `initialFocusRef` call lands,
     and a `fill` — or a keystroke, or a click followed by typing — reaches the
     field. What the caret does **afterwards** has two answers, and the card
     states both, because `PrimaryBlocker`'s own frame (`:505`) decides which
     one runs (decision 1): on the **fast** cold load the grant cancels that
     frame and the field keeps the caret; on the **late** one the frame has
     already run, the blocker's unmount drops the caret to `body`, and the fixed
     tree leaves it exactly there. **The app moves the caret on neither path** —
     that is the property — while the base tree moves it to `#apunta-content`
     on both. Typed text survives the gate, the handoff and every re-render
     behind the window either way, because the value lives in `AddPatient`'s
     state and nothing in this card re-creates that component (decision 1). The
     residual the narrowing admits — the app behind the blocker is in the tab
     order and the accessibility tree for the one `'acquiring'` interval — is
     recorded in the return file in the coordinator's own words (Step 6) rather
     than left implicit, next to the fact that the covering prompt still holds
     pointer and keyboard throughout it.
   - **Rejected, with the reason.** *Deleting the rAF* — it is the keyboard
     landing for a takeover, and decision 3's third case exists to stop that.
     *Re-focusing the name from `AddPatient` when the window becomes primary* —
     that is a second focus call papering over a gate, which is precisely what
     `AddPatient.tsx:39-42` says it refused to do, and it leaves the field
     unfocusable for the fill. *Removing `<Workspace />` from `/patients/new` to
     quieten the storm* — that is the owner's design (2026-09-27), not this
     card's. *Widening the e2e spec's wait* — the spec does not change.
3. **The new test file is the proof; five cases, two of which fail at the base
   and one of which keeps the narrowing honest.** `web/src/App.primaryWindow.test.tsx`,
   all against the real `<App />` and the real `AddPatient`, through
   `installFakeApi`:
   - **(a) The gate, cold.** With a deferred grant, on a cold
     `/patients/new`, the content subtree is **not** `inert` while the phase is
     `'acquiring'`, and the blocker's takeover prompt is still on screen — so
     the case is about the gate, not about removing the prompt. Assert the flag the
     way `App.test.tsx:1515` does (a cast, because `inert` is outside the DOM lib
     in this toolchain) and assert the prompt is there in the same test.
   - **(b) The caret, cold — the case that reproduces the user's loss, pinned to
     the late cold load.** Its three placements are the case's specification, not
     a hint, and each exists because of `PrimaryBlocker`'s frame (Read:
     `:490-509`):
     1. **one animation frame is flushed after the mount**, so the blocker's own
        frame (`:505`) has already run and the state under test is the late cold
        load's rather than the fast one's;
     2. **the case places the caret in the name field itself** — focus it and
        type, the gesture a user makes while the window unblocks — **while the
        phase is still `'acquiring'` and before the grant is released**;
     3. **one more frame is flushed after the release**, before anything is
        asserted, because `becomePrimary`'s rAF at `:270` does its work in a
        frame.
     The file installs its **own** `requestAnimationFrame` stub for this —
     callbacks queued, drained one batch at a time, so "a frame has run" is a
     fact and not a race — exactly as it installs its own deferred Web Locks
     shim, and no shared helper is touched. `vi.useFakeTimers()` with an
     explicit advance is the equivalent and is allowed; either way the assertion
     is taken only after the frame is provably flushed. Then:
     `document.activeElement` **is** the name input, and the typed name is still
     its value. At the base commit the post-release frame focuses
     `#apunta-content` and the case fails on that assertion; on the fixed tree
     nothing runs in that frame, the field is untouched, and it passes. An
     assertion taken inside the releasing `act()` is **not** this case — it
     passes at the base, `test $rc -ne 0` is false, and the row goes red on a
     correct diagnosis. A case that never places the caret in the field is not
     this case either: it would be asserting the blocker's dialog div, which
     this card may not fix (`:490-509`, Must not edit in May edit), and it would
     be red on the fixed tree with no legitimate repair.
   - **(c) The handoff keeps its focus move.** The one case that fails if the
     fix is done by deleting the rAF: take the window blocked and then unblocked
     — hold a **foreign** holder under the app's own lock name,
     `PRIMARY_LOCK_NAME = 'apunta-primary-v1'` (`App.tsx:162`, Read), so the
     app's `ifAvailable` probe answers `null` (`:362-374`) and the phase goes
     `'secondary'`; the fake shim at `fakeApi.ts:412-490` grants an
     `ifAvailable` probe `null` while another holder is held and queues an
     exclusive one until it is released — that is the takeover path — and
     **the holder is released inside the 8 s abort** (`TAKEOVER_TIMEOUT_MS`,
     `:165`, `:388`) or the takeover unwinds and the case never gets a grant.
     Then assert the caret **is** moved into the app. The steal it asserts is
     also a frame — `becomePrimary`'s rAF at `App.tsx:270` — so (c) drains one
     frame of the file's own stub after the takeover grant and only then
     asserts, exactly as (b) does; with the stub installed and no drain, (c)
     fails on the base and on the fixed tree alike, because nothing has run in a
     frame. The existing shape to copy is the unsupported-window case at
     `App.test.tsx:1501-1518` plus the grant control in the new file. A
     **guessed** lock name is the silent no-op this wording exists to prevent:
     the probe would answer `null` for a window that is in fact the only one,
     and (c) would pass at the base **and** after the fix while pinning
     nothing.
   - **(d) A re-render storm does not disturb a typed name.** Type a name on
     `/patients/new`, then drive the recency storm's own shape — a burst of
     re-renders of the workspace behind the window (the `usePatientRecency`
     pattern: many small state updates, `usePatientRecency.ts:63`) — and assert
     the field still holds it and the mark layer still renders it. **This case
     passes before the fix too**, and the card says so: it is the standing guard
     on the property the objective names, not a reproduction. Report it as such
     rather than as evidence.
   - **(e) The gate, blocked — the pin Stop condition 4 needs.** With the same
     foreign holder as (c), the content subtree **is** `inert` while the phase is
     `'secondary'`, and it is still `inert` once the takeover is under way
     (`pending === true`, `:566-579`). This case **passes at the base and must
     pass on the fixed tree**: it is what stops the narrowing becoming "never
     `inert`", and it is the unit-level statement of the guarantee that today
     exists only as a race in `e2e/tests/save-integrity.spec.ts:80` and `:87`,
     where `contentInertScript() === true` is asserted immediately after the
     blocker's prompt is visible — and the prompt is visible during
     `'acquiring'` too, so after decision 2 that assertion no longer implies the
     phase it was written for (in practice the `ifAvailable` probe resolves in a
     microtask, long before Playwright's first poll, so it reads a settled
     `'secondary'`; the narrowing removes the margin that made that
     order-independent). Editing the e2e file is not this card's (Must not
     edit); pinning the state here is, and the pair is what keeps
     `save-integrity.spec.ts` correct by construction. V5 runs it as the e2e
     half.
   - jsdom does not implement `inert`'s focus behaviour, so (a) and (b) assert
     the **cause and the steal** rather than a swallowed keystroke, which is
     exactly why the Playwright citation in decision 1 and the e2e row in
     decision 4 are both load-bearing. A test that tried to reproduce the
     swallow in jsdom would be asserting a thing the environment cannot show.
     (e) needs no browser for the same reason: `inert` as a property is readable
     in jsdom, only its focus behaviour is not.
4. **`spelling.spec.ts` is the acceptance gate, and a failure in it now means
   something specific.** The spec is not edited (Must not edit). V5 runs it
   amplified in a **populated** sandbox, and V6 runs the whole suite five times
   at default workers — S2.R's borrowed row, the same tripwire S2.9 and S2.10
   carried. The difference from those cards' runs is what a failure now means:
   - a failure at `spelling.spec.ts:92` or `:93` on the fixed tree is **the
     card's own row failing**, not a known flake, and the trace is read for the
     two values decision 1 names before anything else is tried;
   - a failure anywhere else in the suite is reported with its file, line and
     message verbatim, and is not fixed here unless it is one of the two May-edit
     paths (Stop condition 7);
   - the passed and skipped counts are recorded from all five runs and must be
     identical across them, with the same structural six skipped
     (`language-control.spec.ts:104`, `:154`, `:203`, `:268`, `:385` in
     `chromium` and `:80` in `es-MX-language`) and nothing new moving into
     `skipped`.
   The `consoleErrors` guard is untouched, so a console error of any class —
   including a recency 404 outside AM-094's one — still fails its test, and the
   recency-404 count is recorded from each run as a number (decision 4 of S2.10,
   unchanged).
5. **No remount-proofing is invented, and the latent reset in `AddPatient.tsx:31`
   is a recorded finding.** `name` is state initialised once from `?name=`
   (`AddPatient.tsx:31`), so a remount *would* lose a typed name — there is just
   no remount (decision 1). The obvious hardening, keeping the name in
   `sessionStorage` or `localStorage`, is **refused here on privacy grounds**:
   `useDocumentTitle.ts:10-13` goes to some length to keep a patient name out of
   the tab title, the window switcher and history, and writing a typed name to
   disk inverts that decision for a field whose whole life is a few seconds. If
   the owner wants drafts to survive a reload, that is a product decision with a
   contract attached, and §6 reserves it. The finding to report is therefore
   precise: *the Add-patient name is not persisted across a reload or a remount,
   deliberately, and the only remount lever in the tree is a pathname change that
   navigates away from the form.* `AddPatient.tsx` does not change.
6. **Isolation, one `sandbox.mjs env`, and the ports.** This card starts servers,
   exactly as the L1 cards S2.1, S2.9, S2.10 and P2.2 do, so the dispatch assigns
   a port from 7800 to 7889 (C-ISO@1 rule 2) and **7717 is never contacted**.
   `npm run e2e` builds the app and starts both servers itself
   (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:115-142`), so **one** `sandbox.mjs env` is the whole
   arrangement: the es-MX server takes `7820 + 1` and `<runFolder>/data-es-MX` on
   its own (`:32-36`). `printEnv` (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs:299-310`) exports no
   `APUNTA_E2E_ES_PORT` and no `APUNTA_E2E_ES_DATA_DIR`, and sourcing a second
   env after the first would move the *English* server onto the second port and
   leave `7820` unused — the trap `reviews/S2.6-ir.md:290-322` filed and
   `reviews/S2.6-postUI-ir.md:54` settled. V5 creates and sources it; **V6
   sources the same file and creates no second env**, which is the one adaptation
   the rows state rather than leave to the reader. `7820` is filled under
   COORDINATOR §6 and is **at most 7888**, because the es-MX server lands on
   `7820 + 1`; V7's own port is **at most 7887** so its es-MX server stays inside
   the same ceiling. Env files go to `/tmp`, never into the checkout
   (RUN-CONFIG §4). Playwright's browsers are not in
   `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md`, so `npx playwright install` is not run; this box
   uses the config's own documented escape hatch,
   `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/chromium`
   (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:57-61`), on every Playwright command. Nothing is
   downloaded (HS-3). Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never
   committed; `docs/v2/evidence/S2.11/` gets the sanitised record
   (`<sandbox>`, `~`).
   **Resuming into a lost env file.** The checkpoint this card runs on is
   `docs/v2/state/cards/S2.11.json` if the coordinator has written it
   (coordinator-owned — read it, never write it; Must not edit), and the other
   half of the resume record is the fixed env path
   `/tmp/apunta-v2-s2.11-e2e.env`. **If that file is gone when V6 starts, V5 is
   re-run from its first command**, which recreates the env *and* repopulates it.
   Re-running `sandbox.mjs env` alone is never the shortcut: it makes a fresh run
   folder, and a fresh sandbox passes `spelling.spec.ts` 6 of 6
   (`reviews/S2.9-impl.md:206-220`), which hides the entire card.
   **Every row runs the pinned Node.** V1 to V7 each open with
   `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/apunta-node/node-v24.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" && `,
   because this box's default is v26.8.2, outside the root
   `engines: ">=24.19.0 <25"`, where 3 of the 6 cases in
   `web/src/lib/appearance.test.ts` fail for a reason no card owns
   (`docs/v2/cards/S2.4.md:306`) — a V4 run on the host Node would be red in both
   zones on a file outside May edit, which is Stop condition 7 for a reason that
   has nothing to do with this card. V8 is the one row that runs no Node, so it
   carries no prefix.
7. **Nothing is skipped, retried or weakened to get a row green, and CI is a
   shape check, never the evidence.** `retries` stays at its config value
   (`:87`, zero outside CI) and the V6 pass condition is **five consecutive
   exit-0 runs at default workers**. In CI `retries: 2` and `workers: 1`
   (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:88`) would mask exactly what this card is about, so
   V7 exists only to prove the fix does not depend on the sandbox — its exit 0
   is a shape check and **may not be quoted as the row's evidence**. The same
   stands for a serial run: `npx playwright test --workers=1` or
   `npm run e2e -- --workers=1` (which npm silently drops,
   `docs/v2/state/reviews/S2.8-impl.md:76-80`) may be run to localise a failure
   and may not be reported as V6.
8. **Two paths in the change set, seen by a command that can see a new file, and
   the stale comments are findings rather than edits.** The check is
   `git status --porcelain` run alongside `git diff --name-only 87b08466794301295dda2c907852b88d15777b73`, and
   both halves are read: `git diff` reports **tracked** paths only, so on its own
   it cannot name `web/src/App.primaryWindow.test.tsx` — this is the first card
   in the S2 sequence whose May edit contains a **new** file, which is exactly
   why the single-command form of the check would be unsatisfiable here — while
   `git status --porcelain` sees the untracked new file and the modified tracked
   one in one output. Between them they must show exactly two paths belonging to
   this card: `web/src/App.tsx` as the modified tracked path and
   `web/src/App.primaryWindow.test.tsx` as the only new untracked path, plus the
   card's two required outputs once Step 6 has written them (AM-017) and nothing
   else. Staging the new file with `git add -N` to make `git diff` print it is
   **not** the answer: it mutates the index the coordinator owns, and `git add -A`
   is forbidden outright (HS-4). Inside `web/src/App.tsx` the diff is decision
   2's two places and nothing else. The comments this card makes untrue —
   `web/src/App.test.tsx:816-819` and `web/src/routes/AddPatient.tsx:39-42` — are
   reported in the return file with their line numbers, for the coordinator and
   the owner, and are **not** edited here (Must not edit; §6). A file outside the
   two is a stop (Stop condition 3).

## Steps

1. **Read, then measure, before any edit.** Read the Read list — including
   `PrimaryBlocker`'s own frame (`:490-509`) and the lock names (`:162-167`),
   because case (b)'s placement and case (c)'s string both come from them. Then
   run V3's negative control *first* — with the new test file written and
   `App.tsx` still at the base version — and record the two failures (a) and (b)
   verbatim. If either passes, Stop condition 1 and the card stops with the
   measurements. A fix written before this is a guess wearing a test's clothes,
   which is the failure mode S2.10's own decision 5 existed to prevent.
2. **Apply decision 2**, the gate and then the caret, in `web/src/App.tsx`, and
   nothing else. Run V2 and V1 as they land.
3. **Run V3 again** on the fixed tree: the new cases pass, the restore is proven
   with `sha256sum -c`, and the two assertions that failed at the base are named
   in the return file as the diagnosis's own receipt.
4. **Run V4** — the whole unit and integration suite in two zones — and V5, the
   amplified `spelling.spec.ts` in the sandbox V5 populates, restoring the P2.2
   screenshots after each Playwright run.
5. **Run V6 last and uninterrupted**: five consecutive default-worker runs of the
   RUN-CONFIG §3 e2e line, one env, the screenshot restore between runs and
   nothing else touching the tree. Record each run's command, exit code, start
   and end time, and passed/skipped counts, and the recency-404 count from each
   (decision 4).
6. **Run V7**, the CI shape, and V8. **Re-run V1's two path commands once the two
   required outputs exist**, so the scope check is read against the finished
   change set rather than a half-written one. Then write
   `docs/v2/state/returns/S2.11.md` and `docs/v2/evidence/S2.11/`: the base-commit
   negative control's output, the two-place diff and why that shape, the new
   cases and what each one proves, the residual decision 2 admits (the app in the
   tab order during `'acquiring'`, with the covering prompt still holding pointer
   and keyboard), the stale-comment findings with their lines, the per-run counts
   from V6, the recency-404 counts, and any failing spec and
   line **verbatim** rather than as a summary. Leave everything uncommitted for
   the coordinator, the P2.2 PNGs among it.

## Why this is a new card, and not an amendment

Recorded so the next reader does not repeat the detour.

- **Not an amendment to S2.10.** S2.10 is `APPROVED`
  (`docs/v2/state/PROGRESS.json`), and an amendment cannot act on an approved
  card. Its own Fixed decision 5 said so at the time: if S2 were confirmed, "the
  remount itself is a **product** question, so report it with the trace and stop
  there" (`docs/v2/cards/S2.10.md:537-540`), and its Must-not-edit list names
  `web/src/routes/AddPatient.tsx` explicitly as a file it may not touch even
  though the diagnosis points at it (`:226-232`).
- **The objective is not reachable inside S2.10's May edit.** Every path in that
  list is under `e2e/`, and the fix is `web/src/App.tsx`. There is no shape of
  this change that a test-only edit reaches, which is the point of decision 1:
  the field is empty because the app will not take the input, and a test cannot
  make the app take it.
- **AM-100 authorised this card and only this card** (`AMENDMENTS.md:123`): "S2.11
  (Parent S2, Depends S2.10) may edit the web code the root cause needs plus a
  regression test; S2.R waits on it." May edit is two web files, which is that
  grant read into paths.
- **Not folded into S2.R.** A parent review edits no code anywhere in this plan,
  and a review's `Depends` is generated from its child list
  (`docs/v2/tools/plan-lib.mjs:parseMilestones`), so `S2.11` is in `S2.R`'s
  children and `S2.R` waits on it automatically — no hand-edited edge, and
  `docs/v2/DEPENDENCIES.md` regenerated by `node docs/v2/tools/check-plan.mjs`
  rather than edited.
- **Findings is `none` on purpose.** The observation came from S2.10's attempt-2
  implementation review (finding 1 of `reviews/S2.10-impl2.md`), which is an
  implementation-review finding, not an R-numbered review finding, so no
  `TRACEABILITY.md` row is added and no R-row's proving column changes — the
  S2.10 precedent at `docs/v2/cards/S2.10.md:10` and `:681-701`.

## Stop conditions

1. **V3's negative control does not fail at the base commit** — either new case
   (a) or (b) passes with `App.tsx` at the base version. Stop and report both
   results verbatim. It means the emptying is not this gate, and decision 1's
   diagnosis is wrong; a fix written on top of that would be a guess, and the
   remount hypothesis would be live again with no evidence behind it either.
   **Before stopping, read the row's own numbers**: (b) passing on the base is
   far more often a placement mistake than a wrong diagnosis — an assertion taken
   inside the releasing `act()`, before the frame that follows the release, reads
   the field on the base tree too (decision 3(b), decision 1). Fix the case and
   re-run; only a case that is placed as decision 3(b) specifies and still passes
   on the base is this stop.
2. **A failing `spelling.spec.ts` run on the fixed tree shows
   `document.getElementById('apunta-content').inert === false` with
   `document.activeElement` on `#patient-name`** at the moment the field reads
   `""`. Stop and report those two values, the run, and the trace. The gate was
   not the cause of that run, the field held the caret, and the value was
   genuinely lost from state — which is a different defect, and §6 reserves it.
3. **The fix needs a third file**, a change to `web/src/App.test.tsx` (any line,
   comment included), any edit to `e2e/tests/spelling.spec.ts`, or any path
   outside the two May-edit ones — on **either** half of V1's check, tracked
   (`git diff --name-only 87b08466794301295dda2c907852b88d15777b73`) or untracked (`git status --porcelain`).
   Stop and report the path and the line. §6 reserves widening to the owner, and
   the stale comments decision 8 names are findings, not edits. Reaching for
   `PrimaryBlocker` (`:490-509`) to restore the caret the late cold load drops is
   the same stop: the case is specified so that no such edit is needed.
4. **The fix changes the gate for a window that is known to be blocked** — the
   `'secondary'` or `'unsupported'` phases, or the takeover focus move itself.
   Stop and report. Those are the single-primary-window behaviour the blocker's
   comment at `App.tsx:74-79` describes, the existing test at
   `web/src/App.test.tsx:1515-1516` records, and decision 3's cases (c) and (e)
   pin — (e) is the one that says `inert` is still set while the phase is
   `'secondary'`, so this stop has a unit-level pin of its own and not only the
   e2e file; a change that trades a second window's protection for a first
   window's convenience is the wrong trade and not this card's to make. Likewise,
   if the gate cannot be narrowed without weakening what is behind the blocker,
   stop with that finding rather than reaching past May edit.
5. **A run leaves `docs/v2/evidence/P2.2/screenshots/` modified, or the fix
   needs `workers: 1`, a retry, a skip, a timeout increase, a weakened
   assertion, an `e2e/playwright.config.ts` edit, a `no-english.ts` edit, or a
   `consoleErrors` narrowing wider than AM-094's single class.** For the
   screenshots, revert and continue — that is routine. For everything else,
   stop and report. A config change hides the defect instead of fixing it, and a
   guard narrowed past the owner's one named class weakens every test in the
   suite.
6. **The evidence puts the cause in `server/` or `shared/`.** Stop and say so
   plainly, with the lines. Those are outside May edit and outside this card, and
   the owner takes them.
7. **V1, V2, V4, V5, V6, V7 or V8 fails in a file outside May edit** — including
   a prettier or ESLint failure on another session's in-flight file. Report it
   and re-run later; do not reformat or fix anything outside May edit. The
   card's own two required outputs are the one exception (AM-017).

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ISO@1 Isolation and the sandbox wrapper

**Built by** P0.3. **Proven by** P0.3 (negative tests) and Q1.1.
**Consumers:** every card that starts a server, opens a real database, runs
e2e, runs `check:format`/`check:refine`, runs a real-model eval or launches
the app.

**Interface** (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs`, Node, no dependencies):

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs run --port <p> -- <cmd...>` | Creates run folder, starts server, verifies ownership, runs `<cmd>` with the sandbox environment, stops only what it started, exits with `<cmd>`'s code |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port <p>` | Creates run folder only, prints `export` lines for tools that start their own server (Playwright) |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs selftest` | Runs the negative cases below; exit 0 only if all refuse correctly |

**Rules**
1. Run folder: `/tmp/apunta-v2/<runId>/` with `data/`, `logs/`, `tmp/`,
   mode `700`. `runId` = UTC timestamp + 8 random hex characters.
   `realpath` of every path must stay under `/tmp/apunta-v2/`; a symlink that
   escapes is refused.
2. Port must be an integer 7800 to 7889 and free (checked by binding, then
   released immediately before the server binds). 7717 is always refused.
   7890 to 7899 are reserved for the updater test server (C-UPD) and refused
   here.
3. The data folder is never the platform default. The wrapper computes the
   default with `platformDataDir()` (C-PATH) **as a string only** and refuses
   if the sandbox path equals it or is inside it. It never lists or opens the
   default.
4. Server environment: `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, `APUNTA_PORT`, `APUNTA_NO_OPEN=1`,
   `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `APUNTA_V2=1`. When `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID` is
   set, `/api/health` includes `"testRunId"`; the field never appears
   otherwise.
5. Ownership check: the wrapper polls `/api/health` for up to 30 s and
   proceeds only if `testRunId` equals its `runId`. Anything else (no
   answer, a different id, no id) is refused and the child is stopped.
6. Child command environment adds `APUNTA_CHECK_URL`, `APUNTA_E2E_PORT`,
   `APUNTA_V2=1`.
7. Cleanup kills only the process group the wrapper created. Never `pkill`,
   never the Ollama daemon.
8. When `APUNTA_V2=1`: Playwright sets `reuseExistingServer: false`;
   `scripts/check-note-format.mjs` and `scripts/check-refine.mjs` exit 2 if
   `APUNTA_CHECK_URL` is unset or points at port 7717.

**Normal example.** `sandbox.mjs run --port 7801 -- npm run check:format`
→ run folder created, server answers with the matching `testRunId`, the
check runs against `http://127.0.0.1:7801`, server stopped, exit code of the
check.

**Rejection examples** (each must be a `selftest` case, refused before any
database is opened): `--port 7717`; `--port 7890`; port in use by a dummy
listener; a dummy server on the port answering `/api/health` with 200 but no
or wrong `testRunId`; run folder symlinked outside `/tmp/apunta-v2/`;
`APUNTA_DATA_DIR` equal to the platform default string.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
